reason: Attack failed on the line, but the evidence locator is wrong and the empty note has to be filled. I read the essay itself twice this run, from two independent full texts rather than from quotation pages: the Are.na selections PDF, which prints the American spelling honor and names its source as On Lies, Secrets and Silence, Selected Prose 1966 to 1978, W. W. Norton, New York, 1979, and the Lesbian History Group PDF, which prints the complete essay with Rich's own headnote and the British spelling honour. Both give the sentence identically, Lying is done with words, and also with silence., comma and full stop included, so there is no wording drift and nothing minted. Attribution is right and the essay is right. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Adrienne Rich at 0 for the year, not banned. The source line is 111 characters, leads with the name, carries no dash and no straight double quote, and the tag Essay is the form of the work. Now the corrections. First, the locator in the evidence is false in both halves. The essay has NO numbered notes; its fragments are separated by asterisk dividers printed as three asterisks. And the sentence is not at the head of the essay. The essay opens with Rich's headnote about where the notes were read, then the parenthetical note beginning These notes are concerned with relationships between and among women, then a run of fragments on the old male idea of honour, the colonial toast, Lovelace, women's honour, and the political lie ending at We are accustomed to the contempt inherent in the political lie. Then the first divider and the single line about being lied to in a personal relationship. Then the second divider, and Lying is done with words, and also with silence. opens the THIRD section, with the woman who tells lies in her personal relationships following it, exactly as the verifier said. So the sentence opens a section, which is a real and citable position, but it is the third section and not the first note and not the head of the essay. Both texts agree on the divider placement, so the count is safe, but because the sections are unnumbered in print I have left the shipped source line alone rather than mint a section number into it; the correction belongs in the note. Second, the note is empty and must not ship empty. Rich's own headnote says the notes were first read at the Hartwick Women Writers' Workshop, founded and directed by Beverly Tanenhaus, at Hartwick College, Oneonta, New York, in June 1975, and were published as a pamphlet by Motheroot Press, Pittsburgh, 1977, and in Heresies, volume 1, number 1. That is a piece read aloud before it was printed, which is the same shape as the Audre Lorde carry in 09-phil-16, and that one carried only because its note says so plainly. This note must say the same, and must say that the wording shipped is that of the 1979 Norton collection named in the source line, since the British reprint respells honour elsewhere in the essay even though it does not touch this sentence.
